text: A v2.19.0 project migrates in one visible commit with refuse-lossy residue named, `project_id` stamped, `.claude/` hooks and settings.json unchanged BY THE MIGRATION VERB and `.claude/settings.json` REWRITTEN TO CANON by the claude-upgrade hop with content outside canon's ownership preserved (`.githooks/**` is AC-10.15), and a git-revert rollback PROCEDURE DOCUMENTED -- **documented, not exercised: AC-10.6 is the exercised one and is unsatisfied** (clauses disambiguated by vc 2026-08-20 17:06Z, on cc's own objection to their position). **BOTH EDITS ARE CLARIFICATIONS AND NEITHER CHANGES WHAT THIS CRITERION DEMANDS.** *hooks* read as including `.githooks/**`, which carries the whole commit gate and which nothing in the estate asserts -- so the clause promised a reader more than any row delivers, and the missing half is now AC-10.15 rather than implied here. And *documented git-revert rollback* sitting in a roll-up beside an unsatisfied AC-10.6 **made this criterion read as covering an exercised rollback when it never did** -- cc's point, put against their own proposal, and the strongest thing said about it. **AMENDED TO THE RULED BEHAVIOUR (hv 2026-08-28 13:26Z, chosen from options vc authored, first-hand in vc's session; recorded on the hv board).** The clause previously read *`.claude/` hooks and settings.json unchanged*, which was true of the pre-canon era and is FALSE of the ruled procedure: the one visible commit covers both hops, and the claude-upgrade hop rewrites `.claude/settings.json` to canon with content outside canon's ownership hand-carried (hv's grant 4 of 2026-08-28 09:09Z). The migration verb itself still leaves `.claude/settings.json` + `.claude/scripts/**` byte-identical, which is AC-10.4's asserted ground and is unchanged by this amendment -- the two claims were one clause and are now two, scoped to the hop each is true of. Measured, not recalled: Conflab's migration commit b02b93c4 carries the settings.json rewrite in the same visible commit as the migration.
